name: What is the best layout for a narrow bathroom?

mainEntity.name: What is the best bathroom layout for a narrow or galley-style bathroom?
mainEntity.text: What is the best bathroom layout for a narrow or galley-style bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: A narrow bathroom works best when the layout prioritizes circulation first and fixture size second. In many cases, placing the vanity and toilet along one wall and keeping the shower or tub at the far end creates the cleanest path. Another option is to use a compact vanity, a sliding or pocket door, and a glass shower enclosure to reduce visual clutter. The biggest mistake is overstuffing the room with oversized fixtures that make the bathroom feel even tighter. In older homes, a narrow bath can often be improved more by smart fixture placement than by adding expensive finishes. A skilled designer will usually study door swing, sight lines, and traffic flow before choosing the final arrangement.
acceptedAnswer.description: In a narrow bathroom, the best layout usually keeps the fixtures on one side or splits them logically to preserve a clear walking path. The goal is to avoid blocking the door swing, maintain usable clearance, and place the shower or tub where the room feels widest.
